From “The Songs of Bilitis”CXL. The Last Lover

By Pierre Louÿs (1870–1925)

 
(1894. Translated from the French by Horace Manchester Brown. 1904)
C
OME,
 boy, pass me not by without having first loved me. I am still beautiful in the night. Thou shalt see that my autumn is warmer than the spring-time of another.
  1

  Seek not for love among virgins. Love is a difficult art in which young girls are little learned. I have studied it all my life in order to give it to my last lover.
  2

  My last lover, that shall be thou, I know it. Behold my mouth, for which an entire people has paled with desire. Behold my hair, the same hair that Psappha the Great has sung.
  3

  I will gather in thy favor all that is left of my lost youth. I will destroy the memories themselves. I will give to thee the flute of Lykas, the girdle of Mnasidika.
  4
